{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZcjxOg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDDx7U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 57, "title": "Implement V30 BOUND/CHKIND with next-instruction vector-5 return semantics", "body": "## Problem

The VM profile stops with a host error when valid DOS guest code executes V30 `BOUND` (`CHKIND`, opcode `62h`). This leaves a documented CPU instruction unavailable even though operand decoding, interrupt entry and IRET already exist.

At baseline `9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6`, the opcode handler explicitly returns `unimplemented V30 BOUND`; Ap instead performs a bounds check and raises restartable exception 5. Simply removing the VM rejection would incorrectly give V30 the Ap return-address behavior. See [the opcode handler](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6/src/cpu.rs#L1114) and [fault restoration in Cpu::step](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6/src/cpu.rs#L633).

## Expected outcome

Implement valid VM `BOUND r16, m16&16` execution in original Rust, including guest-visible vector-5 delivery and return.

The hardware contract is:

- Decode `62 /r` with a 16-bit register index and two consecutive little-endian memory words: lower bound first, upper bound second. Compare signed values; both endpoints are inclusive. Successful execution preserves registers, bounds and flags. NEC specifies the operand layout and conditional BRK 5 operation in its [V-series Instruction Manual, printed pp. 52–53](https://www.ardent-tool.com/CPU/docs/NEC/V20-V30/v_series.pdf#page=63); Intel explicitly documents the [signed BOUND comparison](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/05au-cs240c/lab/i386/BOUND.htm).
- An out-of-range VM index invokes vector 5 regardless of IF. Read its IP/CS from physical `00014h`–`00017h`, push the original FLAGS, CS and **next-instruction IP** as words, and clear IF/TF. Ordinary IRET resumes after the instruction without modifying the saved IP. NEC describes the [vector and entry sequence in Section 6](https://www.ceibo.com/eng/datasheets/NEC-V20-V30-Users-Manual.pdf); its instruction manual defines CHKIND as BRK 5 and explains that [PC advances as instruction bytes are consumed, Appendix A.4](https://www.ardent-tool.com/CPU/docs/NEC/V20-V30/v_series.pdf#page=196). The next-instruction interpretation follows those documented operations.
- Preserve Ap's existing 16/32-bit behavior: out-of-range BOUND remains a fault whose saved address identifies the instruction, including its first prefix. Intel explicitly distinguishes this [restart address](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/05au-cs240c/lab/i386/BOUND.htm).

Scope is this instruction and its profile-specific event delivery. Reuse existing addressing, Bus mapping and interrupt machinery. Preserve VM default-SS selection and segment overrides. Register-only second operands are outside documented V30 scope: retain an explicit diagnostic rather than inventing V30 exception-6 behavior.

Non-goals: other V30 instructions, general exception redesign, NMI/single-step implementation, protected mode, paging, x87, instruction-cycle fidelity, application-specific workarounds or compatibility claims.

## Context and reproduction

A minimal original reproduction can initialize VM execution at `0000:1000`, SP=`9000h`, AX=`0005h`, and memory words at `2000h`/`2002h` to `0000h`/`000Ah`, then execute bytes `62 06 00 20`. Source inspection predicts the current host error; expected execution reaches IP=`1004h` with unchanged architectural data. Setting AX=`000Bh` should enter a guest-installed vector-5 handler, whose unmodified IRET returns to `1004h`.

Relevant existing tests are [VM interrupt/IRET coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6/tests/core.rs#L104) and [Ap exception helpers](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6/tests/cpu386.rs#L3). The inspected CPU tests contain no dedicated BOUND acceptance.

Project progress: merged PR #56 fixes duplicate PIT latch retention. The Coordinator reports nine focused tests, 225 native integration tests and 86 production-Wasm browser tests passing; these were not rerun by this evaluator. Independent review and remote CI remain unestablished by the supplied report. See [the validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9bec0af9db768ecd2d6b3b466a0bbe3b1bfb5cc6/docs/validation.md#issue-55-ordinary-counter-latch-retention-2026-10-24). All 26 inventory statuses and fixed scopes remain unchanged. No open Issue or completed improvement in the supplied history duplicates this task.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add original `v30_bound_` Rust tests in `tests/core.rs`. Demonstrate the minimal valid reproduction fails against unchanged production code and passes after implementation; record the actual outcomes.
- [ ] Test lower/equal/interior/upper/outside cases, negative and mixed-sign ranges, `8000h`/`7FFFh`, equal bounds and reversed bounds. Exercise every index-register encoding, including SP evaluated before interrupt pushes.
- [ ] Cover direct and indexed addressing, displacement forms, BP-based default SS, all four segment overrides, unaligned bounds and effective-address arithmetic wrapping. Use distinct data in competing segments and guards to detect wrong reads or writes.
- [ ] For both below-range and above-range VM cases, assert the exact six-byte frame, nonzero saved CS, next IP including a segment prefix, pre-entry FLAGS, IF/TF clearing, IF-independent delivery and unchanged bounds. Execute a guest IRET and prove exactly one handler invocation followed by forward progress. Confine memory changes to the expected frame and deliberate guest results.
- [ ] Add focused `bound_` tests in `tests/cpu386.rs` preserving Ap word/dword signed comparisons, size/address overrides, restart at the first prefix, guest repair followed by IRET/retry, register-operand rejection and LOCK rejection. Preserve existing segment-limit behavior.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built VM boot probe, for example `guest/v30_bound.asm`, an offline preparation script and a checked manifest recording source/license, assembly command, source/boot/image hashes, expected results/guards and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget. Include preparation in README and existing CI; keep generated fixtures outside `web/`. Acquire no proprietary software or ROMs.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe image natively and through the production release-Wasm browser artifact at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset. Require explicit PASS, no FAIL/core/browser errors, exact guest-produced results/guards and unchanged disk bytes. The guest must validate the frame and return behavior; the host only advances execution and observes results.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the new preparation command, `cargo test --locked --test core v30_bound_`, `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 bound_`, and the README's complete applicable fixture/provenance, Rust, formatting, Clippy and production-Wasm/browser checks. Preserve all existing hardware, DOS/application, VM and six-game regressions, fixtures, assertions and budgets. Report exact commands, outcomes and any temporary server-port substitutions.
- [ ] Update the V30 implementation boundary and validation record with specifications and actual evidence. V30 remains **partial**: packed-BCD strings, bit-field extensions, TF single-step, NMI and broader instruction/fault acceptance remain outstanding. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 retain their fixed required scope. Limited probes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
